_doc: Deterministic supply-chain rule pack (spec 007, R7). Structural manifest evaluation - offline only; guard evidence is tri-state and resolution behavior that lives outside the repo is recorded as undetermined, never assumed. 'suspicious-package' names match case-normalized exact names; matched values are never serialized into findings.

rules.title: Internal-namespace package resolvable publicly without a demonstrated guard
rules.description: The project depends on an internal-looking package name, but no in-repo guard (registry index pinning or lockfile) demonstrates that resolution cannot fall back to a public registry - the dependency-confusion vector.
rules.recommendation: Pin the internal index in repo configuration and commit a lockfile; alternatively claim the name publicly.

rules.title: Scoped internal package without a demonstrated private-registry mapping
rules.description: A scoped package bearing an internal namespace has no demonstrated @scope registry mapping (.npmrc) or lockfile-resolved origin in the repository, so a namesake on the public registry can be resolved instead.
rules.recommendation: Map the scope to the private registry in .npmrc and commit the lockfile.

rules.title: Mutable dependency reference without a committed lockfile
rules.description: A dependency is declared with a mutable or absent version constraint while no lockfile pins the resolved artifact, so subsequent installs can fetch substituted content.
rules.recommendation: Pin an exact version and commit the ecosystem lockfile.

rules.title: Unpinned dependency without a committed lockfile
rules.description: A Python dependency is declared without an exact pin and no lockfile (uv.lock/pylock.toml/Pipfile.lock) pins the resolution, so substituted content can be fetched.
rules.recommendation: Pin exact versions (==) and commit the lockfile.

rules.title: Dependency matches a known typosquat/confusion-prone name
rules.description: The declared package name exactly matches an entry in the offline suspicious-name dataset (typosquatting / brandjacking shapes).
rules.recommendation: Verify the intended package name and provenance; replace with the legitimate package.
